The Akwa Ibom State Police Command has arrested two men and recovered substances suspected to be hard drugs and about N22,000 during a raid on a suspected criminal hideout in Ibeno Local Government Area. The operation was carried out at about 6:00 p.m. on November 26, 2026, at Mkpanak Village, following a targeted raid on identified black spots in the area. The state Police Public Relations Officer, Timfon John, disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday in Uyo. John identified the suspects as Solomon Akpan, 30, of Eket Local Government Area, and Auwal Bashir, 31, of Kaduna State, adding that other suspects fled when they saw the operatives. The statement read, “The Akwa Ibom State Police Command has intensified its crackdown on criminal hideouts, following a targeted raid on identified black spots at Mkpanak Village, Ibeno Local Government Area, resulting in the arrest of two suspects and the recovery of substances suspected to be hard drugs and cash. Other suspects reportedly fled upon sighting the operatives.” Police arrest two with hard drugs in Akwa Ibom FG gives flood-hit Akwa Ibom farmers inputs FG unveils blue economy innovation hub at UNIUYO The police said the suspects were in custody, while investigations were ongoing to establish their alleged involvement and apprehend the fleeing suspects. “The arrested suspects are in custody, while investigations are ongoing to establish their alleged involvement and apprehend other fleeing suspects,” the statement added. The state Commissioner of Police, Baba Azare, reiterated the command’s commitment to sustaining intelligence-led operations, dismantling criminal hideouts and preventing illicit drug activities and other crimes. He urged members of the public to provide credible information to assist security agencies in the fight against crime. “We will continue to sustain intelligence-led operations, dismantle criminal hideouts, and ensure that individuals involved in illicit drug activities and other criminal enterprises have no haven in Akwa Ibom State,” he added.
